topic: Set Claude up the right way so it becomes your daily work tool: Claude is several tools in one app (Cowork, the model menu, Claude for Excel, plugins and skills, artifacts, projects), when to use each, a first prompt and one tip for each, where Claude falls short, and your first 30 minutes
audience: Professionals who already chat with Claude now and then and want it to become the tool they open every working day
goal: Know which part of Claude to reach for, set each part up once, and finish a 30-minute set-up: settings, model, one project, one artifact, one plugin, one Cowork task or the Excel add-in
notes: Claude can be used on the web at claude.ai, in Claude Desktop for Mac or Windows, and in Claude for iOS or Android. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114491-get-started-with-claude]

In Claude Desktop, chat is available on every plan including Free, while Claude Code and Claude Cowork require Pro, Max, Ultra, Team or Enterprise. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10065433-install-claude-desktop]

Claude Cowork brings Claude Code's agentic capabilities to knowledge work beyond coding, using the same agentic architecture with no terminal required. Instead of answering prompts one at a time, Claude takes on multi-step tasks and carries them out for you: you describe an outcome, step away and come back to finished work, such as formatted documents, organised files and synthesised research. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Cowork is on paid plans only: Claude Desktop (macOS, Windows, Linux beta) on all paid plans; web and mobile on Pro, Max, Ultra and Team (beta on Team), and Enterprise when an owner enables it. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

To start a Cowork session: open Claude on the web, in Claude Desktop or in the mobile app; in the message box, select 'Cowork'; describe the task; review Claude's approach, then let it run. To go back to a regular conversation, select 'Chat'. If the message box no longer shows 'Chat' and 'Cowork' options, you have the new Claude experience and every conversation can take on a Cowork task. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

In the new Claude experience, chat and Cowork are merged into one conversation with no mode to choose; it is rolling out to Pro, Max and Ultra, and once moved you cannot switch back. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16761823-claude-cowork-and-chat-are-one-claude]

Cowork runs sessions remotely in the cloud, so sessions and files follow your Claude account across desktop, web and mobile, and work continues when you close your laptop. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Cowork tasks run in an isolated, temporary environment on Anthropic's servers; local files opened through the desktop app are processed on Anthropic's servers. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13364135-use-claude-cowork-safely]

On desktop, Cowork can read from and write to your local files without manual uploads or downloads; local files, the browser and computer use need the Claude Desktop app open. Cowork can produce Excel spreadsheets with working formulas, PowerPoint presentations and formatted documents. You can jump in to course-correct or give more direction mid-task. Before Claude permanently deletes any files, you see a permission prompt and must select 'Allow'. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]

Cowork analyses your request and makes a plan, breaks complex work into subtasks, and delivers finished outputs to your session, where you can preview and download them. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]
Cowork can produce spreadsheets and slides that can be further edited with Claude for Excel and PowerPoint. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13345190-get-started-with-claude-cowork]
By default Claude asks before permanently deleting files, but that protection does not cover computer use. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16761823-claude-cowork-and-chat-are-one-claude]

Scheduled tasks, which run a saved prompt on a recurring basis or on demand, are available on all paid plans in Cowork and the new Claude experience. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13854387-schedule-recurring-tasks-in-claude-cowork]

Anthropic warns that Cowork has unique risks because of its agentic nature and internet access, and that write tools carry more risk than read tools. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13364135-use-claude-cowork-safely]

The current model lineup: Claude Fable 5.2 (demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work), Opus 5.5 (long-running agentic coding and knowledge work), Sonnet 5.5 (best combination of speed and intelligence) and Haiku 5.5 (high-volume, latency-sensitive tasks). Anthropic's docs advise starting with Opus 5.5 if unsure. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview]
Comparative latency: Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5 are 'Moderate', Sonnet 5.5 'Fast', Haiku 5.5 'Fastest'. [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview]

Anthropic recommends starting most coding and knowledge tasks with Opus 5.5 as the 'strongest daily driver', moving up to Fable or Mythos or down to Sonnet 5.5 or Haiku 5.5 as needed. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2]

Anthropic positions Sonnet 5.5 as strongest at well-scoped everyday tasks and at creating polished documents, slides and spreadsheets, while Opus 5.5 is for complex work needing careful judgment. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5]
Claude Haiku 5.5 is Anthropic's cheapest and fastest small model, built for high-volume work. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-haiku-5-5]
On the Free plan, the pricing table shows Sonnet and Haiku as available, but not Opus or Fable; Opus is available on Pro, Max and Ultra. [https://claude.com/pricing]

Fable models are on all paid plans: on Max, Ultra and Team or Enterprise premium seats you can spend up to 50% of weekly limits on them; on Pro and Team standard seats they run on usage credits. Fable is not on Free. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15424964-claude-fable-models-on-your-plan]

Claude Sonnet 4.6 leaves the model selector on Free, Pro, Max and Ultra on December 8, 2026, with Sonnet 5.5 recommended as the replacement. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/18537562-claude-sonnet-4-6-is-leaving-the-model-selector]

The model menu next to the send button controls the model, the effort level and thinking. To change the model, click the model name next to the send button and pick a model, or click 'More models'. To change effort, click the model name, click 'Effort' and choose a level. Each model's recommended level is marked 'Default'. Low and Medium suit routine tasks and stretch your usage further; High is the best balance of quality and speed; Extra high is for long-running coding and agentic tasks; Max is the most thorough. You can change the model or effort at any point in a conversation, and changes apply from Claude's next response. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8664678-change-the-model-effort-and-thinking-settings]
The selected model is shown below the text input on web and desktop and at the top of the screen on mobile. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114491-get-started-with-claude]

Effort levels in the app are Low, Medium, High, Extra high (xhigh, Opus 4.7 and newer) and Max; higher effort takes longer and uses more of your limits. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8664678-change-the-model-effort-and-thinking-settings]
In Claude Code and the Claude apps the default effort is Medium, while the Claude Platform (API) defaults to High. [https://www.anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5]

Claude for Microsoft 365 works inside Excel, PowerPoint, Word and Outlook, and claude.com says these add-ins are generally available on all paid Claude plans. [https://claude.com/claude-for-microsoft-365]

Claude for Excel answers questions about your workbook with cell-level citations, adjusts assumptions while keeping formulas intact, finds and fixes errors, and builds or fills in models. It can sort, filter, edit pivot tables, apply conditional formatting and create data validation dropdowns. It runs on Excel on the web, Excel on Windows with Microsoft 365 (build 16.0.13127.20296 or later) and Excel on Mac (16.46 or later). [https://claude.com/docs/office-agents/excel]
In Claude for Excel, answers include cell-level citations you can click to go to the referenced cell. [https://claude.com/docs/office-agents/excel]

Install Claude for Excel: go to the 'Claude for Microsoft 365' listing on Microsoft AppSource and select 'Get it now'; open Excel, activate the add-in (Home > Add-ins on Windows, Tools > Add-ins on Mac) and sign in with your Claude account. Anthropic's Claude for Excel page links to the listing. [https://claude.com/docs/office-agents/excel]

In Claude for Excel, Settings in the add-in sidebar has an Instructions field for preferences that apply to every conversation in Excel only. Claude warns you before overwriting existing data. Use of the add-in counts toward your Claude account's usage limits. [https://claude.com/docs/office-agents/excel]

Claude for Excel limits: not recommended for final client deliverables without human review or for audit-critical calculations without verification; data tables, macros and VBA are not supported; it does not run on Excel 2016 or 2019 perpetual licences, Excel on iPad or Excel on Android. Only use it with trusted spreadsheets, because files from outside can hide instructions (prompt injection). Best practice: start with a trusted copy of the workbook, be specific about what you want changed, and review changes. [https://claude.com/docs/office-agents/excel]

Known issue: after the September and October 2026 Microsoft 365 updates on Windows, some users are missing chat history and uploaded skills in the Claude add-in. [https://claude.com/docs/office-agents/excel]

Plugins bundle skills, connectors and sub-agents into one package, so you get a ready-to-go set-up for your role from the first conversation. They are on all paid plans. Install: open Customize in the left sidebar (it brings plugins, skills and connectors together), open the Plugins tab, open the Discover tab, select a plugin and click 'Add'. The library covers sales, finance, legal, marketing, HR, engineering, design, operations, data analysis and more; Plugin Create helps you build your own. Type '/' or click '+' to see the skills from your plugins. Plugins may include local MCP servers that run on your computer, so only install plugins from sources you trust. Plugins you add follow you to chat, Cowork and Claude Code. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13837440-use-plugins-in-claude]
A plugin's local MCP server runs on your computer with the same permissions as any other program you run. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13837440-use-plugins-in-claude]

Skills are folders of instructions, scripts and resources that Claude loads dynamically for specialised tasks; they are available on all plans and need code execution turned on. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512176-what-are-skills]

Anthropic's built-in skills handle Excel, Word, PowerPoint and PDF creation and are used automatically when relevant. To add your own skill, package the skill folder as a ZIP, go to Customize > Skills, click '+', then '+ Create skill' and 'Upload a skill'. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-use-skills-in-claude]

Connectors let Claude access your apps and services, retrieve data and take actions, with each person's own permissions. Browse them from a chat via '+' > 'Connectors' > 'Manage connectors', or from Customize > Connectors. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11176164-use-connectors-to-extend-claude-s-capabilities]

An artifact is anything Claude makes that you'd put in front of someone (a design, deck, document, dashboard or small interactive tool); it opens beside the conversation, and you can edit it and share it. Artifacts are on all plans. Templates: Docs, Slides and Design on all plans; Data on paid plans; Sheets and Whiteboards in beta on paid plans; Motion in beta on Team and Enterprise. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17153992-what-are-artifacts-and-how-do-i-use-them]

Start an artifact by asking for one in any chat, by selecting 'Output' in the message box and choosing a template, or from the Artifacts tab in the sidebar, where everything you make is saved. In a doc, highlight the text you want changed, click 'Edit with Claude' and type your request. Docs export to Word, PDF, Markdown and Google Docs; Slides can be edited slide by slide, presented inside Claude and exported to PowerPoint or PDF. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17153992-what-are-artifacts-and-how-do-i-use-them]

In an artifact made from a template you can edit directly, for example by typing in a doc. With 'Edit with Claude', Claude makes the edit where you marked it, so you don't have to describe which section you mean. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17153992-what-are-artifacts-and-how-do-i-use-them]

Artifacts need the code execution and file creation setting ('Create and edit files' in the updated layout) turned on in Settings > Capabilities. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/17153992-what-are-artifacts-and-how-do-i-use-them]

Code execution and file creation is available to all users on web, desktop and mobile, is on by default for Free, Pro, Max and Ultra, and lets Claude generate Excel, PowerPoint, Word and PDF files. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12111783-create-and-edit-files-with-claude]

Projects are self-contained workspaces with their own chat histories and knowledge bases; they are available to all users, and Free users can create up to five. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9517075-what-are-projects]

Memory is on by default for Free, Pro, Max and Ultra; Claude saves memory as individual topics as you chat, can be told to 'remember this', and keeps a separate memory for each project. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11817273-use-claude-s-chat-search-and-memory-to-build-on-previous-context]

Create a project: click 'Projects' on the left side, or go to claude.ai/projects; click '+ New Project' in the upper right; give it a name and description (Claude does not see these). The knowledge base is on the right of the project's page: click '+' to add files. Click 'Set project instructions', write how Claude should work, then 'Save instructions'. Context is not shared across chats in a project unless it is added to the project knowledge. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9519177-how-can-i-create-and-manage-projects]
Project content is cached and counts less against usage limits when reused; caches expire after inactivity. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices]

Account-wide Instructions are set in Settings > Your Claude > Instructions and apply to all conversations; project instructions apply within a project. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10185728-understanding-claude-s-personalization-features]

Web search is turned on in a chat with '+' > 'Web search' and answers with citations; in the new Claude experience there is no toggle and Claude searches when it helps. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10684626-enable-and-use-web-search]

Claude can 'hallucinate' incorrect or misleading information; Anthropic says not to rely on it as a single source of truth, and to scrutinise high-stakes advice and check cited sources. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8525154-claude-is-providing-incorrect-or-misleading-responses-what-s-going-on]

Claude can hallucinate its own capabilities, such as claiming to have sent emails; it has no access to tools that are not explicitly connected. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241188-claude-is-producing-links-that-don-t-work-and-falsely-claiming-that-it-has-sent-emails-or-produced-external-documents-what-s-going-on]

Claude does not generate photos or illustrations like image-generation tools; it builds diagrams, charts and interactive visuals with HTML and SVG, and can analyse images you upload. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9002504-can-claude-produce-images]

Models may not know about events after their training cutoff, which is June 2026 for Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114494-how-up-to-date-is-claude-s-training-data]
Claude analyses images and charts only in PDFs of 100 pages or fewer; for longer PDFs it reads the text only. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8241126-upload-files-to-claude]

Most accounts have a usage limit that resets on a rolling five-hour session window, paid plans add weekly limits, and use across web, desktop, mobile and Claude Code draws from one pool with no fixed message count. [https://claude.com/pricing]

The five-hour period starts with your first message; remaining usage is shown under Current session in Settings > Usage. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11647753-how-do-usage-and-length-limits-work]

Things that use limits faster include message length, attachment size, conversation length, tool use (Research, web search), model choice, effort level, artifacts and multi-step tasks. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9797557-usage-limit-best-practices]
Anthropic names prompt injection, hidden instructions in web content, as the biggest risk for AI that uses a browser. [https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12902428-use-claude-in-chrome-safely]
Mojeed Abisiga is a data and AI leader and educator whose mission is to make data and AI easy for everyone; he teaches people to use AI at work. [https://mojeedabisiga.com/]
